req_desc: The product is a public marketing site with a signed-in account surface for a coding agent sold to developers ...
Every public marketing route is readable without an account.
One benchmark registry feeds the leaderboard, the two model routes, the calculator, with no route holding its own copy of a figure.
A signed-out visitor may read every public route ...
A direct API call from a member session to an owner-only endpoint is denied by the server, leaving the protected state unchanged.
Signup is open to anyone from the signup route.
Three accounts are seeded: `owner@example.com`, `member@example.com`, `owner2@example.com` ...
An account is created by posting an address, a password, a display name to the signup endpoint ...
A signup whose address is already registered is rejected as invalid, creating no second account.
A signin with a wrong password is denied, returning no token ...
A request to an account route without a valid bearer token is denied.
An expired token on an account route sends the browser to the signin route carrying the address the browser was trying to reach.
A return address that is not a path on the product own origin is discarded, so signin lands on the account overview.
Every marketing route carries the same fixed bar ...
The footer compliance line names four certifications separated by vertical bars, reading SOC 2, ISO27001, ISO42001, AIUC-1 Certified ...
Six footer destinations that leave the origin are marked as leaving, opening in a new context.
Every internal link on every public route resolves.
The home headline reads `Marlin is your coding agent for building ambitious software.` ...
At a narrow width the home primary control reads `Get started`, dropping the platform name.
The install block carries two tabs, `PowerShell`, `Linux / WSL`, with the first selected ...
The home changelog band renders the four most recent entries, date, title only, from the same source as the changelog route ...
The home changelog band closing link reads `See what's new in Marlin`.
Six product routes share one template, differing only in content ...
A product route is a content document, so a seventh route requires no new component.
The automations route renders six template cards from the same marketplace source as the six seeded automations ...
The teams route headline reads `Your best engineer's setup, for everyone`.
The teams route control leads to checkout when the visitor owns a workspace, to workspace creation when the visitor owns none, to signup when signed out ...
The enterprise route headline reads `Develop enduring software at scale`.
The enterprise customer-proportion claim is stored data carrying a source, an as-of date ...
There is no self-serve purchase path for the enterprise plan.
The changelog route is one column of entries, newest first, each carrying a date, a title, a standfirst, a body ...
The model registry holds fifteen rows, each with a code, a name, a provider, a benchmark figure, a cost per task, tokens per task, steps per task ...
The benchmark plot horizontal axis descends left to right, placing the cheapest model at the right edge.
The leaderboard carries fifteen rows ranked by the benchmark figure descending, each with a colour dot tying the row to its plot series.
The leaderboard unit switch offers three choices with the first selected ...
The model `glim-7b` carries no measured cost per task ...
A self-reported benchmark figure is marked in the accessible name of its cell, not only in a note beneath the table.
The benchmark plot carries a written description naming every model plotted in the chart.
The vendor model route uses the display face for exactly one word.
The partner model route renders from the same registry, never from a hand-authored figure.
The calculator computes in the browser, submitting nothing, storing nothing.
The calculator allocation must total exactly `100`, so a total that does not reach one hundred suppresses the outputs ...
No floating-point arithmetic touches money at any step of the calculator.
With `Kestrel 4` at `40`, `Meridian 4` at `60`, the blended cost per task is `$8.33` ...
On the worked example the tasks view reads `480` against `231`.
A shift to a more expensive model produces a negative saving, displayed as a loss, never as zero.
A model with no cost per task is absent from both calculator selects, from the allocation rows.
The calculator is prefilled with a plausible spend, a default pair of models ...
The catalogue holds sixteen published entries of two kinds ...
The catalogue listing endpoint accepts a query, a kind, a category, a sort, a page, a page size ...
The popularity ordering breaks a tie on the slug ascending.
A catalogue search is reflected in the address, so returning to the address reproduces the result set.
A catalogue detail route renders the tile, the name, the publisher, the full description, the category, the version, an install control ...
Installing is idempotent on the pair of subject, plugin, so a second call creates no second installation ...
A signed-out visitor using an install control is sent to signin, returning to the entry afterwards.
A card description is truncated by a fade at its edge, never by an ellipsis, never by a server-side cut.
An empty catalogue search echoes the query, still rendering the featured section beneath.
Eight platform rows exist at three versions, with no `linux` `armv7` `deb` artifact at `3.18`.
Resolution is a pure function from operating system, architecture, format, channel to one artifact ...
Resolution never blocks rendering, so the control renders with a neutral label, resolving in place.
An unknown platform resolves to a page listing every artifact, never to a guess.
Every artifact carries a checksum displayed beside the control ...
A missing artifact for a resolved platform offers the previous version marked as older, never a different platform.
A download is recorded on resolution, carrying operating system, architecture, format, version, channel, referring route ...
Four plans carry seven purchasable tiers ...
A capability granted at a lower tier order within a plan is granted at every higher order ...
The interval switch changes the displayed price, the interval carried into checkout ...
The questions band is headed `Questions & Answers`, carrying four disclosures ...
A signed-in visitor sees the current tier marked as current, with its control reading as a management action.
Checkout creates the workspace billing account in the payment platform under a pinned external key ...
A second checkout for the same workspace creates no second billing account, leaving exactly one account with that external key.
A checkout that would produce a second live subscription for one subject is rejected as a conflict.
The product never shows a billing outcome the product has not read back from the payment platform ...
A tier upgrade within a plan is immediate, prorated for the remainder of the period ...
Creating a workspace mints a slug from the name, making the caller its first owner with a seat.
An owner invites a colleague by posting an address, a role to the workspace invitation endpoint ...
The invitation subject begins `Marlin invitation:` followed by a space, the workspace name ...
Inviting an address that already holds a pending invitation re-sends the same acceptance link, creating no second invitation.
Revoking an invitation sends no message ...
Accepting an invitation turns the pending row into an active membership, consuming one seat ...
A member calling the invitation endpoint directly is denied, creating no invitation, sending no message.
Removing a member releases the seat, revoking that member sessions at once ...
A request for another workspace members, usage answers as not found rather than as denied ...
Recording usage requires an owner, taking an idempotency key, a model code, a surface, a task count.
The rated cost is the task count multiplied by the model cost per task in integer minor units ...
Replaying a usage request with the same idempotency key adds no second row, changing no total ...
Each usage event carries two timestamps, one for when the usage happened, one for when the product recorded the usage ...
The usage endpoint returns the included allowance, the consumed amount, the overage, a breakdown by model, by member, by surface ...
The seeded workspace `aurora-data` reads `8869` consumed against `8000` included, leaving `869` of overage ...
An owner sets, clears the workspace spend limit in minor units.
Usage past the spend limit is refused with a distinct answer naming the limit ...
Nothing is deleted for non-payment, so members, usage, installations, settings survive a lapsed subscription.
The account overview shows the current tier, the period usage against the allowance, the workspace.
An anonymous request for an account route lands on signin carrying the requested path.
An account belonging to no workspace sees workspace areas absent rather than disabled.
A member sees the members area as a read-only list with no invitation control.
The four legal routes share one template with a heading, an updated line, a contents list, an anchored body.
The security route carries seven sections in a fixed order beginning with certifications, ending with vulnerability disclosures.
Each certification carries an issuing body, a scope, a validity window, an evidence address ...
The contents list is generated from the body headings, never authored.
An anchor target sits clear of the fixed bar.
Step one of the sales form collects exactly two fields ...
A free-address provider is refused on the work address field with an explanation ...
Validation runs on blur for a field the visitor has left, on submit for everything ...
A submission suspected of being automated is accepted, stored, flagged, never refused ...
The enquiry source is a closed set of four values with a fallback.
Submitting the same enquiry twice produces a confirmation both times, one stored enquiry.
An address matching no route renders the product own not-found page inside the full chrome, answering as not found ...
A removed thing answers as gone, saying the thing has been removed ...
Every public route carries its own title, its own description, with no two routes sharing either.
A site map lists every public route, with a robots file pointing at the site map.
Nothing the browser downloads contains a credential, an interface key, an administrative token.
Every route named in the brief route table is reachable.
Signin with no return path lands on the account overview ...
A visitor can reach the calculator from the footer, set an allocation, read the saving.
A visitor can sign up from the pricing route, create a workspace, confirm checkout, land on the billing area.
An owner can invite a colleague, with the pending row appearing in place in the member list ...
A signed-in visitor can filter the catalogue by category, sort by popularity, install an entry.
Every list has an empty state naming what is absent, offering a way back ...
The page ground is a near-white warm neutral, nearer unbleached paper than white ...
The primary control carries the strongest contrast in the product, taking the foreground colour ...
Everything is set in one humanist grotesque carrying a variable axis of stroke thickness ...
The marketplace tile corner is a proportional curve on a square rather than a fixed radius.
Motion is eased throughout, with one speed for a state change, one for an entrance, one for an exit ...
Contrast meets WCAG AA in both themes, verified independently ...
The layout answers to roughly six widths, holding at every width between them ...
The theme control offers three states with system as the default ...
The drawn window carries a frame, a title bar, inner panes holding real text.
The task list groups rows under two headings, each carrying a count.
The chat pane renders a sequence of labelled agent steps, with the running step carrying the shimmer.
The caret is a solid block one line tall rather than a thin line.
When two windows overlap the front takes the heavier shadow, the one behind takes a hairline ring alone ...
The wallpaper is generated rather than photographed, carrying grain, a vertical softening.
Every glyph is drawn as inline vector, never loaded as a font.
The mobile route uses one translucent layered surface treatment found nowhere else.
No route depends on a binary image, a recorded video, an icon font arriving.
An element animates once on first entering view, never reversing when scrolled back past ...
The application is server-rendered, so every document arrives as complete markup from the server ...
The three backing services are already running, so none is downloaded, installed, compiled, started ...
Only the six named payment-platform paths are used, with refunds, payment methods, chargebacks out of reach.
A bearer token is read from the authorization header on every account route, every mutating endpoint ...
Money is an integer number of minor units at every layer, formatted once at the edge.
Every response carries the standard security headers.
Every state-changing request carries an origin check failing closed on a missing header ...
Server-side validation runs for every request regardless of what the browser already checked ...
Fourteen tables exist, with every timestamp in UTC.
Every seeded account uses the password `deku-demo-pw-2026`, written into `/app/USER_README.md`.
The users table carries a unique address compared without regard to case.
The workspaces table carries a unique slug, a tier code, a seat count, a nullable spend limit, a nullable billing external key.
One membership exists per workspace, per user ...
One pending invitation exists per workspace, per address at a time.
Seven tier rows exist carrying a plan code, an order within the plan, a monthly price, a yearly price, a per-seat flag, an included allowance.
One entitlement row exists per tier, per capability ...
At most one subscription row per subject is in a live state at any instant ...
The model series ordering is stable, never assigned by iteration order.
One catalogue row exists per kind, per slug ...
One installation row exists per subject, per plugin.
Twenty-three release artifact rows exist, one per version, operating system, architecture, format.
The usage table is append-only with an idempotency key unique across the table ...
The consumed amount reconciles exactly with the sum of the rated costs over the period.
A row carrying a workspace reference is readable only by an account holding an active membership in that workspace ...
The seeded workspaces are `Aurora Data` with slug `aurora-data`, `Northlight` with slug `northlight` ...
One product, one origin, with no separate documentation application, no separate help centre ...
The app must be reachable at `APP_PUBLIC_URL` ...
Every graded endpoint carries the request shape, the return shape named in the interface table ...
The billing account is the payment platform record rather than a row the product wrote to itself ...
